newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan forces say key rebel naval base smashed.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan forces say key rebel naval base smashed.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops launched a sea and air attack on a northern rebel "Sea Tiger" naval base killing or wounding as many as 40 guerrillas, military officials said on Monday.
Sri Lankan forces lost five dead and five wounded in Sunday's four-hour assault against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam's (LTTE) naval wing, a military spokesman said.
"We hammered the base in a combined operation," he said. "Troops withdrew after destroying the base."
The navy also lost two boats in the attack on the Poonaithoduwai Sea Tiger base near the Jaffna peninsula, about 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital Colombo, officials said.
The LTTE could not be immediately reached for comment.

Rebel Voice of Tigers radio, monitored by Reuters, said air force planes carried out several bombing runs near Poonaithoduwai while navy gunboats offshore provided gunfire support during an amphibious landing.
One civilian was killed while several others were wounded, it said.
There was no way to verify the rebel claim independently as the government bans journalists from the war zone.
Five Sri Lankan sailors, including two officers, were killed and five soldiers wounded during the assault, the military spokesman said.
The spokesman said he was not immediately aware of rebel casualties but a navy official said up to 40 LTTE rebels were believed killed or wounded.
Army special forces were landed by helicopter while the navy's Special Boat Squadron made an amphibious landing using shallow draught water-jet propelled boats, he said.
Army guns from a nearby base and navy gunboats offshore provided covering fire during the assault, military officials said.
The navy suffered its casualties when rebels destroyed a small water-jet boat with rocket-propelled grenades, they said.
One grenade struck another boat but failed to explode and was subsequently detonated by sailors badly damaging the craft, they said.
Army chief Lieutenant-General Rohan Daluwatte was quoted in the independent Island newspaper as saying the rebel base housed more than 1,000 guerrillas.
"This operation was conducted mainly to cripple the Sea Tiger strength in that area," he said.
The Sea Tigers have emerged as a major threat to the navy and military convoys taking troops and supplies to bases in the north.

Sunday's raid was the first major military offensive since last month's capture by the army of the rebel stronghold of Kilinochchi, the last major town held by the LTTE after the military regained control of the northern Jaffna peninsula in April.
The rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
